plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SMH, SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
This plan focuses on de-risking the portfolio by eliminating high-beta and leveraged positions.
It prioritizes income and broad index exposure for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative approach targets a potential ~1.5%/month return, emphasizing capital preservation. It aims for lower volatility and reduced drawdown risk by cutting all leveraged exposure and high-loss positions.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name mandate.
Sell SMH entirely due to its significant loss and downtrend.
Reduce exposure to other leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to small positions.
This strategy balances broad index and quality tech with a small, controlled amount of leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets a potential ~2.5%/month return, focusing on risk-first growth. It aims to reduce overall portfolio concentration and leverage while maintaining some exposure to growth opportunities.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name mandate.
Sell SMH due to its significant loss and downtrend, reallocating capital.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to lean into potential growth.
This strategy concentrates in high-beta and leveraged positions for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth approach targets a potential ~4%/month return, but comes with significantly higher risk. Expect larger drawdowns and be aware that leveraged ETFs experience daily decay and rebalancing, which can erode value quickly. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
Sell all high-beta and leveraged ETFs (SMH, SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to near zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
It aims to create a cash-like income stream with reduced market exposure.
income.read: This income approach targets a potential ~1%/month return, focusing on parking cash for yield. While aiming for reliable distributions and low drawdown, remember that distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in market selloffs. This is not a savings account.
